samples.summary: The new `levelOf` normalization protects only the planner; the layout pass still reads `listLevel` raw, where a non-finite value throws a RangeError and takes the whole layout down
samples.evidence: `list-level.ts` normalizes at "the single point of read" and its own comment concedes the layout "reads `listLevel` raw" — but the unprotected reader is worse than bad geometry. `packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts:1091` does `levelCounters.length = Math.max(levelCounters.length, level + 1)` with `const level = block.listLevel ?? 0` (line 1089). With `level = NaN` that assignment is `arr.length = NaN` → `RangeError: Invalid array length` out of `computeLayout`; with a large finite level (> 2^32-1) the same. `layout.ts:494` also multiplies it into the indent. The value is reachable unvalidated: `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:495` does `block.listLevel = Number(attrs.listLevel)` on a peer's Tree attribute, and `packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:178` serializes whatever the content ingest supplies (`String(block.listLevel)`, no clamp, no schema bound anywhere in packages/backend/src). The diff's claim that a poisoned level is "repaired by the gesture that touches it" cannot hold here: layout runs on first render, before any gesture. Fix belongs on the raw readers (reuse the new `levelOf`/`MAX_LIST_LEVEL` in `layout.ts`), not on the planner.
searchedFor: packages/backend/src grep listLevel (only docs-tree.ts:178, seed builders)

samples.summary: The centralized indent ceiling is bypassed by the PPTX importer, which writes `listLevel` straight from the file with no clamp
samples.evidence: The diff promotes `MAX_LIST_LEVEL` to a shared model export whose stated job is to keep "a payload from inventing a level" — but that clamp lives only in `packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:351`. `packages/slides/src/import/pptx/text.ts:268` assigns `block.listLevel = list.level` where `list.level` comes from `const level = pPr ? (attrInt(pPr, 'lvl') ?? 0) : 0` (line 314) with no bound at all, so an untrusted `.pptx` seeds an out-of-band level into a Block that the docs text-box editor and the docs layout then consume. Slides already depends on @wafflebase/docs (it imports `initializeTextBox`), so the new export is reachable from the importer. Note the sibling exporter documents the field as untrusted for exactly this reason (`packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:77-85`).

samples.summary: The list-level ceiling is still hardcoded as a literal `8` in the slides PPTX exporter, now that the same value is an exported shared constant
samples.evidence: `packages/slides/src/export/pptx/text.ts:85` is `return ` lvl="${Math.min(8, n)}"``, with a docstring at :77 restating the `[0, 8]` range. The diff's whole move is to make `MAX_LIST_LEVEL` (`packages/docs/src/model/list-level.ts:7`) the one definition — this literal (and the doc text at `docs/design/docs/docs.md:162`, which spells the number out) is the duplicate left behind, and slides already imports from @wafflebase/docs. Nothing breaks today; it drifts the next time the ceiling moves.

samples.summary: `TextEditor.siblingsOf` resolves the parent table with throwing `getBlock`, where its `editor.ts` twin deliberately uses non-throwing `findBlock` for the same stale-map reason
samples.evidence: The new `editor.ts` helper documents the contract explicitly: "Resolved with `findBlock`, not `getBlock`: the map is only as fresh as the last layout pass, so a table removed since then would throw out of the middle of an indent gesture rather than degrade to the block alone" (`packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1632-1634`). The `text-editor.ts` copy of the same helper instead calls `this.doc.getBlock(info.tableBlockId)`, and its `getCellInfo` (`text-editor.ts:3666`) reads `getActiveLayout().blockParentMap` — the stale-by-construction map the editor.ts comment is about. `Doc.getBlock` throws (`model/document.ts:215`). Reachability is limited (the preceding `doc.getBlock(cursor.position.blockId)` would usually throw first for a deleted region), which is why this is low confidence; the fix is one word on the new code.

verdict.reason: Verified the raw readers and searched for any normalizing hop; none exists. layout.ts:1089-1091 reads `block.listLevel ?? 0` and assigns `levelCounters.length = Math.max(len, level+1)`, which throws RangeError for NaN or a level above 2^32-1; layout.ts:494 multiplies the same raw value into the indent. computeListCounters runs on the render path (doc-canvas.ts:242) and in PDF export (pdf-exporter.ts:124), so it executes before any gesture could invoke the new planner normalization (list-level.ts:29-33). The value reaches there unvalidated: crdt-tree.ts:243 and frontend yorkie-doc-store.ts:494-496 both do a bare `Number(attrs.listLevel)`, backend docs-tree.ts:178 serializes `String(block.listLevel)` verbatim, and the authenticated PUT validator in docs-content.controller.ts (assertValidBlock 429-512, assertValidBlockStyle 380-427) validates ids, types, style numerics, spacing markers and inlines but never listLevel/listKind. The only clamp in the codebase is the clipboard paste sanitizer (clipboard.ts:348-351), which is not on the CRDT read path, and there is no migrate/sanitize/normalize hop on the frontend load path (no other MAX_LIST_LEVEL consumers). Impact at the found site is a RangeError out of the layout pass — the whole document fails to render for every viewer, not just the writer — so major is appropriate; the fix belongs on the raw readers, reusing levelOf/MAX_LIST_LEVEL.

finding.summary: New crash path: TextEditor.siblingsOf resolves the parent table with doc.getBlock (throws), unlike the editor.ts twin which deliberately uses findBlock
finding.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2890 `const tableBlock = this.doc.getBlock(info.tableBlockId);` — `getCellInfo` reads `getActiveLayout().blockParentMap`, which is only as fresh as the last layout pass. This file already treats that map as routinely stale: packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2971-2978 wraps arrow handling in try/catch with the comment "Stale blockParentMap data (e.g. table rows removed by remote edit)", and `Doc.getBlock` throws when the id no longer resolves (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:220-266 / findBlock returning undefined). `handleTab` (2699-2707), `handleIndent` (2762) and `handleOutdent` (2779) have no such guard, and before this change the cursor-only path never consulted the parent map at all — so a Tab/Cmd+] with the caret in a cell of a table deleted by a peer now throws out of the keydown handler mid-gesture. The diff's own editor.ts copy documents the opposite choice (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1632-1641, `findBlock`, "rather than throw out of the middle of an indent gesture"); the fix belongs on the new text-editor.ts code (use findBlock + optional chaining).

verdict.reason: Verified in the repo. TextEditor.siblingsOf resolves the parent table with the throwing Doc.getBlock (text-editor.ts:2893) from a layout-pass-only parent map (getCellInfo -> getActiveLayout().blockParentMap, text-editor.ts:3666-3671), while the twin helper in editor.ts:1636-1645 deliberately uses non-throwing doc.findBlock and documents the reason ("would throw out of the middle of an indent gesture"). Doc.getBlock throws (model/document.ts:199-216); findBlock returns undefined (221-231). Reaching callers are unguarded: handleIndent (2760-2775) and handleOutdent (2777-2794), bound to Cmd+] / Cmd+[ at text-editor.ts:1306-1317, go through forEachBlockInSelection's cursor-only fallback (2878-2879) into siblingsOf with no try/catch, unlike handleArrow which explicitly wraps for stale blockParentMap data (2971-2978). handleTab does gate in-cell carets via isInCell (2682, 3662-3664), but the Cmd+]/Cmd+[ paths do not. Only softening found: the same fallback already calls throwing getBlock on the cursor block at 2878, so the window where 2893 throws first is narrower than stated - but that is a co-located unguarded throw, not a guard, so it does not make 2893 unreachable. Finding's line number is off by three (2893, not 2890); substance is accurate. No not-present, already-guarded, or counterexample ground available.
